hello.note: Said with palms pressed together. More formal: नमस्कार (namaskaar).

goodbye.note: नमस्ते (namaste) also works when leaving. अलविदा (alvida) is only for final, dramatic farewells.

please.note: Formal. In speech, politeness usually comes from the -iye verb ending (बैठिए, baithiye) or English 'please'.

youre_welcome.note: Hindi has no set reply to thanks; this ('it's nothing') is the natural one.

yes.note: Politer: जी हाँ (ji haan) or just जी (ji).

no.note: Politer: जी नहीं (ji nahin). Casual: ना (na).

sorry.note: English 'sorry' (सॉरी) is also very common in everyday speech.

excuse_me.note: Literally 'please listen' — the usual way to call a stranger or a waiter.

good_morning.note: Formal. Day to day, people say नमस्ते (namaste) or गुड मॉर्निंग (good morning).

how_are_you.note: To a woman: आप कैसी हैं? (aap kaisi hain?)

im_fine.note: To ask back: और आप? (aur aap?)

whats_your_name.note: Extra respectful, e.g. to an elder: आपका शुभ नाम? (aapka shubh naam?)

my_name_is.note: The verb है (hai, 'is') comes at the end, after the name.

nice_to_meet_you.note: Also common: आपसे मिलकर अच्छा लगा (aapse milkar achchha laga).

im_from.note: से (se, 'from') comes after the place: मैं भारत से हूँ (main Bhaarat se hoon).

speak_english.note: Literally 'does English come to you?' Many people say इंग्लिश (english) instead of अंग्रेज़ी.

dont_understand.note: To ask for a repeat: फिर से बोलिए (phir se boliye).

speak_slowly.note: In speech often without कृपया — the -iye ending is already polite.

where.note: ँ (chandrabindu) nasalises the vowel: the n in kahan is not fully pronounced.

what.note: On its own it can sound blunt; to ask someone to repeat, say जी? (ji?).

how_much.note: Also: इसका दाम क्या है? (iska daam kya hai?)

where_bathroom.note: Also common: बाथरूम (bathroom), वॉशरूम (washroom). Signs say शौचालय (shauchaalay).

can_you_help.text: क्या आप मेरी मदद कर सकते हैं?
can_you_help.roman: kya aap meri madad kar sakte hain?
can_you_help.note: To a woman: क्या आप मेरी मदद कर सकती हैं? (kya aap meri madad kar sakti hain?)

what_time.note: Very common too: टाइम क्या हुआ है? (time kya hua hai?)

six.note: Devanagari digit: ६. Usually pronounced 'chhe'; also spelled छः.

eight.note: Devanagari digit: ८. ठ is a tongue-curled t with a puff of air, not English 'th'.

tea.note: Order it as एक चाय (ek chai); it comes with milk and sugar unless you ask otherwise.

bread.note: रोटी is Indian flatbread. Sliced loaf bread is ब्रेड (bread) or डबल रोटी (double roti).

menu_please.note: Literally 'please show the menu'. Many say मेन्यू कार्ड (menu card).

delicious.note: Very common in speech: बहुत टेस्टी है! (bahut tasty hai!)

no_meat.note: A woman says: मैं मांस नहीं खाती (main maans nahin khaati). Also: मैं शाकाहारी हूँ (main shaakaahaari hoon).

enjoy_meal.note: Hindi has no fixed 'bon appétit'; hosts say this. Formal: भोजन का आनंद लीजिए (bhojan ka aanand lijiye).

left.note: Turn left: बाएँ मुड़िए (baayen mudiye). Drivers also say लेफ़्ट (left).

right.note: Turn right: दाएँ मुड़िए (daayen mudiye). Drivers also say राइट (right).

stop_here.note: Drivers are often called भैया (bhaiya, 'brother'): भैया, यहीं रोक दीजिए.

airport.note: In everyday speech most people say एयरपोर्ट (airport).

hotel.note: In many places होटल can also mean a simple restaurant.

want_to_go.note: No word for 'to' is needed: मुझे दिल्ली जाना है (mujhe Dilli jaana hai).

is_it_far.note: How far is it? कितनी दूर है? (kitni door hai?)

one_ticket.note: Return ticket: आने-जाने का टिकट (aane-jaane ka ticket).

too_expensive.note: When bargaining, add: थोड़ा कम कीजिए (thoda kam kijiye), 'bring it down a bit'.

cheaper.note: Also: कुछ सस्ता दिखाइए (kuchh sasta dikhaaiye), 'show me something cheaper'.

id_like_this.note: When buying, also: यह दे दीजिए (yeh de dijiye).

just_looking.note: A woman says: मैं बस देख रही हूँ (main bas dekh rahi hoon).

pay_card.text: क्या कार्ड से पेमेंट हो सकता है?
pay_card.roman: kya card se payment ho sakta hai?
pay_card.note: Casual and very common: कार्ड चलेगा? (card chalega?)

cash.note: In speech, कैश (cash) is just as common.

open.note: Many shop signs in India simply say OPEN in English.

big.note: बड़ी (badi) with feminine nouns. ड़ is a quick flap of the tongue, between d and r.

tomorrow.note: Same word as 'yesterday'; the verb tense decides: कल मिलेंगे (kal milenge) = see you tomorrow.

yesterday.note: Same word as 'tomorrow'; the verb tense decides: कल बारिश हुई (kal baarish hui) = it rained yesterday.

now.note: अभी is 'right now'; अब (ab) is 'now' as in 'from now on'.

good_evening.note: Formal (TV, speeches). In daily life people just say नमस्ते (namaste) in the evening too.

good_night.note: In everyday speech: गुड नाइट (good night).

see_you_later.note: Also: फिर मिलते हैं (phir milte hain).

call_police.note: Polite form: पुलिस को बुलाइए (police ko bulaaiye). Emergency number in India: 112.

need_doctor.note: Also: डॉक्टर को बुलाइए (doctor ko bulaaiye), 'please call a doctor'.

im_lost.note: A woman says: मैं रास्ता भटक गई हूँ (main raasta bhatak gayi hoon).

pharmacy.note: Signs usually say केमिस्ट (chemist) or मेडिकल स्टोर (medical store).

lost_phone.note: If it was stolen: मेरा फ़ोन चोरी हो गया है (mera phone chori ho gaya hai).

be_careful.note: Also: संभलकर! (sambhalkar!). Warning signs say सावधान (saavdhaan).

no_problem.note: Also very common: कोई बात नहीं (koi baat nahin).

dont_know.note: Shorter and casual: पता नहीं (pata nahin).

i_like_it.note: Also: मुझे अच्छा लगा (mujhe achchha laga), 'I liked it'.

im_tired.note: A woman says: मैं थक गई हूँ (main thak gayi hoon).

welcome.note: Warm and very common at the door: आइए, आइए! (aaiye, aaiye!)
